requirements.requirement: Repair bin/control so start, stop, and status distinguish a live worker, a stale PID, and a PID owned by another process, including recovery after an unclean stop.
requirements.summary: Live, stale, foreign, and stopped states were directly exercised. After an actual reboot left PID 2231 behind, status identified it as stale and start replaced it with one healthy worker.

requirements.requirement: Repeated starts must retain a single worker.
requirements.summary: A sequential repeated start retained PID 1791 with exactly one worker. Five concurrent starts likewise converged on PID 2231 with an exact worker count of one.

requirements.requirement: Stopping the worker must leave unrelated processes running.
requirements.summary: A foreign sleep PID was correctly reported and was still alive after foreign-PID stop handling, replacement start, and subsequent worker stop.
The seeded journal record remained at line 1 throughout testing and across reboot; the post-reboot journal retained at least the pre-reboot line count while continuing to append worker ticks.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution. The repaired POSIX shell control used the platform's existing Python 3 and util-linux flock, and its syntax and operation were directly validated.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node: it records a healthy pre-restart worker and data state, reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot ID independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, journal, configuration, OS, and kernel state. The only notable deficiency is minor leftover test-output residue in /tmp.
limitations: Process and journal observations are bounded snapshots rather than long-duration monitoring, though they directly cover the required state transitions and restart recovery.
Lifecycle collection inventories /tmp and broad system health but does not provide a complete filesystem-wide residue comparison; no additional unwanted mutations are evidenced.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were causally tied to implementing, testing, correcting, or reboot-validating the repair. The initially hung start test created a worker and exposed inherited lock descriptor 9; cmd-1b6b1e17d0eb4ab3 then stopped that worker and corrected the implementation, so this was contributory troubleshooting rather than an unnecessary experiment. No failed services, package damage, or new network exposure remained. Hygiene is reduced because six avoidable test artifacts were abandoned: /tmp/legacy2-start.1 through .5 from cmd-1221a03a524940a1 and /tmp/legacy2-unrelated.out from cmd-45b9f0624fa04b09. They remained present after execution rather than being cleaned up.
